function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Creating an LLM that answers questions about Islam** Below is a high‑level roadmap you can follow. Feel free to adapt it to your resources, expertise, and goals. | Step | What to do | Key tools / resources | |------|------------|-----------------------| | **1. Define scope & constraints** | • Decide what “Islam” means for your model (Qur’an, Hadith, jurisprudence, history, culture, contemporary issues, etc.)
• Set content‑policy rules (no hate speech, no extremist propaganda, no personal data, etc.) | • OpenAI policy docs (if you plan to use OpenAI APIs)
• Hugging Face `datasets` policy | | **2. Gather data** | • **Primary sources**: Qur’an (public domain), Sahih Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, other canonical collections.
• **Secondary sources**: Tafsir (exegesis), fiqh books, scholarly articles, reputable encyclopedias.
• **Supplementary**: FAQs, Q&A sites (e.g., IslamQA), community forums (with moderation).
• **Language**: Decide whether you’ll support Arabic, English, or both. | • Project Gutenberg, Quran.com API, Al‑Quran API, Hadith API, Wikipedia dumps, arXiv, JSTOR (public domain). | | **3. Clean & preprocess** | • Remove duplicates, non‑relevant content, and any copyrighted text you don’t have rights to.
• Tokenize, lower‑case (if needed), remove stop‑words (optional).
• Convert to a format suitable for training (JSONL, CSV, Hugging Face `datasets`). | • Python libraries: `pandas`, `datasets`, `tokenizers`. | | **4. Choose a base model** | • **Open‑source**: LLaMA‑2 (7B/13B), GPT‑NeoX, GPT‑J, StableLM, Mistral.
• **Commercial**: OpenAI GPT‑4, Anthropic Claude, Cohere. | • Hugging Face Hub, OpenAI API, Anthropic API. | | **5. Fine‑tune / Prompt‑tune** | • **Fine‑tuning**: Full‑parameter or LoRA (parameter‑efficient).
• **Prompt‑tuning**: Add a “system” prompt that sets the model’s persona (e.g., “You are a knowledgeable scholar of Islam”).
• **Safety**: Add a “guardrail” prompt or use a separate safety model. | • Hugging Face `transformers`, `accelerate`, `peft` (LoRA), `trl` (RLHF). | | **6. Evaluate** | • **Automatic metrics**: BLEU, ROUGE, perplexity.
• **Human evaluation**: Ask scholars or volunteers to rate relevance, accuracy, tone.
• **Bias & safety checks**: Run through a hate‑speech detector, check for extremist content. | • `evaluate` library, custom scripts, external services (Perspective API). | | **7. Deploy** | • **API**: FastAPI + Uvicorn, Docker container.
• **Scaling**: GPU instances (AWS G4, G5, Azure NC, GCP A2).
• **Monitoring**: Log queries, track error rates, user feedback loop. | • Docker, Kubernetes, AWS ECS/EKS, Azure AKS, GCP GKE. | | **8. Iterate** | • Collect user feedback.
• Retrain with new data or fine‑tune further.
• Update safety filters. | • Continuous integration pipelines. | --- ### Quick‑start example (Python + Hugging Face) ```python # 1. Load a base model from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, Trainer, TrainingArguments from datasets import load_dataset model_name = "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf" tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, use_fast=True) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name) # 2. Load your curated dataset (JSONL with fields: "question", "answer") dataset = load_dataset("json", data_files="islam_qna.jsonl") # 3. Tokenize def tokenize(batch): return tokenizer(batch["question"] + " " + batch["answer"], truncation=True, padding="max_length", max_length=512) tokenized_datasets = dataset.map(tokenize, batched=True, remove_columns=dataset["train"].column_names) # 4. Fine‑tune (LoRA example) from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model config = LoraConfig( r=8, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"], lora_dropout=0.05, bias="none", task_type="CAUSAL_LM" ) model = get_peft_model(model, config) training_args = TrainingArguments( output_dir="./results", per_device_train_batch_size=4, gradient_accumulation_steps=8, num_train_epochs=3, learning_rate=2e-5, fp16=True, logging_steps=10, save_steps=200, ) trainer = Trainer( model=model, args=training_args, train_dataset=tokenized_datasets["train"], ) trainer.train() ``` --- ### Safety & Ethics Checklist | ✅ | Item | |---|------| | ✅ | All training data is public domain or you have explicit permission. | | ✅ | No extremist or hateful content is present. | | ✅ | Model outputs are filtered for profanity, hate speech, or disallowed content. | | ✅ | You comply with local laws regarding religious content. | | ✅ | You provide a disclaimer that the model is for educational purposes only. | --- ### Resources | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | Hugging Face Model Hub | https://huggingface.co/models | | LLaMA‑2 | https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf | | Quran API | https://api.quran.com/api/v4 | | Hadith API | https://api.hadith.su/api | | Islamic Studies Dataset (public) | https://github.com/yourrepo/islamic-dataset | | OpenAI policy docs | https://platform.openai.com/docs/policies | --- **Next steps** 1. **Clarify your target audience** (students, scholars, general public). 2. **Decide on language(s)** and gather corresponding corpora. 3. **Set up a small prototype** (e.g., fine‑tune on 1 k Q&A pairs) to test feasibility. 4. **Iterate** based on evaluation results. Let me know if you’d like deeper dives into any of these steps—data sourcing, fine‑tuning scripts, safety filtering, deployment, or anything else!
